  Code of Ethics

As City of Irwindale Parks & Recreation Commissioners, our fundamental duty is to serve the public good. We are
committed to the principle of an efficient and professional local government. We will be exemplary in obeying the letter
and spirit of Local, State and Federal laws and City policies affecting the operation of the government and in our private
life. We will be independent and impartial in our judgment and actions.

We will work for the common good of the City of Irwindale community and not for any private or personal interest. We
will endeavor to treat all people with respect and civility. We will commit to observe the highest standards of morality
and integrity, and to faithfully discharge the duties of our office regardless of personal consideration. We shall refrain
from abusive conduct, personal charges or verbal attacks upon the character or motives of others.

We will inform ourselves on public issues, listen attentively to public discussions before the body, and focus on the
business at hand. We will base our decisions on the merit and substance of that business. We will be fair and equitable
in all actions, claims or transactions. We shall not use our official position to influence government decisions in which
we have a financial interest or where we have a personal relationship that could present a conflict of interest, or create
a perception of a conflict of interest.

We shall not take advantage of services or opportunities for personal gain by virtue of our public office that are not
available to the public in general. We shall refrain from accepting gifts, favors or promises of future benefit that might
compromise our independence of judgment or action or give the appearance of being compromised.

We will behave in a manner that does not bring discredit or embarrassment to the City of Irwindale. We will be honest
in thought and deed in both our personal and official lives.

Ultimate responsibility for complying with this Code of Ethics rests with the individual elected official. In addition to any
other penalty as provided by law, violation of this Code of Ethics may be used as a basis for disciplinary action or censure
of a Commissioner.

These things we hereby pledge to do in the interest and purposes for which our government has been established .

ITEM NO. 2A  AQUATICS SEASON EXTENSION
AQUATICS SEASON
EXTENSION

MANAGER ZEPEDA  Manager Zepeda presented the staff report. She noted, however, that
  the Assistant Pool Manager is not sure whether she will be available
  to serve during the proposed morning sessions since she has found
  other employment. She plans to update management on Friday with
  regard to her availability. If a lifeguard is unavailable during morning
  sessions, staff recommends that the Commission propose to
  implement afternoon sessions.

COMMISSIONER  Responding to several questions by Commissioner Lopez, Manager
LOPEZ  Zepeda advised that heating the pool does incur costs. However, the
  costs in heating the pool during the proposed extension would not
  impact the budget since they would largely be cancelled out by the
  savings that were realized when the pool was closed recently due to
  inclement air conditions.

ASSISTANT CITY  Assistant City Manager Olivares added that the heating costs would
MANAGER OLIVARES  be absorbed by the existing Fiscal Year 20/21 budget.

COMMISSIONER  Commissioner Roman suggested that the proposed extension be
ROMAN  implemented immediately, to which Chair Fraijo said that this would
  be difficult since staff needs to provide adequate notice to the
  community.

ASSISTANT CITY  Assistant City Manager Olivares agreed with Chair Fraijo and noted
MANAGER OLIVARES  that staff typically coordinates sending notices to residents to provide
  them with at least two weeks' notice before programs commence. She
  also said that staff could potentially begin the extended program
  during the last week of October, though this would have to be done
  carefully due to the ongoing pandemic.

SUZANNE GOMEZ  Suzanne Gomez suggested that a Recreation Supervisor be trained
  as a lifeguard so that they can cover the morning pool sessions. She
  also thanked Recreation staff for how wonderfully they are running
  their programs.

MOTION  A motion was made by Chair Fraijo, seconded by Commissioner Diaz,
  to recommend that the City Council approve a two-week extension for
  pool programs, to begin as soon as possible with both morning and
  afternoon sessions depending on lifeguard availability. The motion
  was unanimously approved.

COMMISSIONER  Commissioner Roman suggested tabling this matter until staff and the
ROMAN  City Council could make a recommendation to the Commission . She
  also requested a budget showing proposed line-by-line expenditures
  for Recreation programs.

CHAIR FRAIJO  Chair Fraijo noted that funding is not currently allocated to many
  upcoming Recreational activities, and spoke against tabling this
  matter since these scheduled events need to be funded .

  Chair Fraijo also requested clarification regarding the Fiscal Year
  20/21 budget, to which Assistant City Manager Olivares explained that
  the COVID-19 pandemic forced all city departments, including
  Recreation, Library, and the Senior Center, to drastically cut their
  budgets, due in part to the County Health Order prohibiting large
  gatherings and events. However, the donation by the Irwindale
  Community Foundation will help fund programs for these departments
  in the upcoming fiscal year. The City Council tabled discussing funding
  recreation programs so that the Commission would have the
  opportunity to provide input and report back to the Council. She then
  advised that, without a recommendation from the Commission, staff
  would probably not have funding for the events that have already been
  planned .

  Chair Fraijo spoke on the need for continued Commission input on
  budgetary items concerning the Recreation Department, and
  suggested recommending approval of the Irwindale Community
  Foundation's donation to the Recreation Department.

MANAGER RODRIGUEZ Manager Rodriguez noted that all city departments had cut their
  budgets, which Chair Fraijo acknowledged.

CHAIR FRAIJO  Chair Fraijo expressed her gratitude for the Foundation's donation to
  continue City programs. She stated that she takes pride in that the City
  of Irwindale has always been able to continue offering programs and
  activities at times when other cities were unable to.

COMMISSIONER  Commissioner Lopez stated that she did not understand why funding
LOPEZ  to programs have been cut since she was not aware of any local
  businesses that have shut down due to the Coronavirus, to which
  Assistant City Manager Olivares indicated that the state has offered a
  deferment of sales tax payments and other revenue streams, which
  have impacted the City's operational capacity. She spoke on the
  uncertainty surrounding the pandemic and its effects on the city
  budget, but added that staff continues to monitor the matter and
  provides routine updates to the City Council.

  Commissioner Lopez stated that she does not want the City to have
  to rely on Foundation donations in order to operate its regular
  programs, to which Assistant City Manager Olivares advised that this
  is not staff's intent, though she pointed out that this is a solution that
  is available at this time. She added that staff is not proposing
  implementing any new programs at this time, and highlighted staff's
  creativity in offering new, free programs for the community's
  enjoyment.

COMMISSIONER  Commissioner Roman suggested spending funding on another
ROMAN  community food drive, to which Assistant City Manager Olivares
  clarified that the previous food drive was organized by the Irwindale
  Community Foundation, not the City. Commissioner Roman also
  spoke against the donation being used to fund the ongoing operation
  of programs, to which Assistant City Manager Olivares advised that
  the donation would not be used toward staff costs or benefits; rather,
  it would be used to fund events and activities.

SUZANNE GOMEZ  Suzanne Gomez expressed concern that funds that had been
  allocated previously for recreation programs were pulled due to the
  pandemic, and requested that the Commission continue working to
  ensure funding for programs that meet the needs of the community.

COMMISSIONER  Commissioner Lopez stated her belief that the Commission is not
LOPEZ  being updated as to recreation programs and funding.

CHAIR FRAIJO  Responding to a comment by Chair Fraijo, Assistant City Manager
  Olivares advised that the Recreation budget was prepared under
  circumstances wherein large gatherings were prohibited. However,
  new health orders are being emanated where certain activities are
  now being permitted. Therefore, staff re-analyzed which activities
  could be implemented anew, and searched for available funding
  sources. The Irwindale Community Foundation had indicated that it
  was willing to provide funding for community events. She also advised
  that staff requested that the Council permit staff to present information
  relating to the Foundation's donation to the Commission for its input
  prior to the Council making a determination on how the funding should
  be used.
